he.text: אלהינו ואלהי אבותינו אָדָם בְּקוּם עָלֵינוּ חִיל אֲחָזַתְנוּ לִרְעוֹד · בְּהִסְתַּפְּחוֹ לְמַלְכוּת חָנֵף כִּמְעַט כָּשַׁלְנוּ לִמְעוֹד · גָּמְרוּ לְמָכְרֵנוּ כְּחֹל וְחָרִיץ בְּלִי מִסְעוֹד · אָמְרוּ לְכוּ וְנַכְחִידֵם מִגּוֹי וְלֹא־יִזָּכֵר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹד׃ דָּלוּ עֵינַי לְמָרוֹם קְרָאתִיךָ אוֹיְבַי לָקוֹב · הַכְרֵת שֵׁם וּשְׁאָר וּמְחֵה זִכְרוֹ לִרְקוֹב · וְצַר צוֹרְרַי בְּנִכְלֵיהֶם אֲשֶׁר־נִכְּלוּ לְעַקּוֹב · וַיֹּאמְרוּ לֹא יִרְאֶה יָּהּ וְלֹא־יָבִין אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב׃ זֵרִים עִנָּה וְיִגָּה וְלֹא מִלֵּב לְכַלּוֹתָם · חָבוּ לְפָנִים וּרְדָם בַּהֲסָרַת טַבַּעַת לְהַחֲלוֹתָם · טוּב דְּבָרוֹ הֵקִים לְעֵינֵי הַגּוֹיִם לְעַלּוֹתָם · בְּאֶרֶץ אוֹיְבֵיהֶם לֹא־מְאַסְתִּים וְלֹא־גְעַלְתִּים לְכַלֹּתָם׃ יָדַע רָמַז הַקּוֹרוֹת לְעָם מְפֻזָּר וּמְפֹרָדִים · כְּתַב הַסְתֵּר אַסְתִּיר וּמָר דְּרוֹר מְפֹרָדִים · לִשְׁבּוֹת הָמָן מִמָּחֳרָת הַמָּן הָעֵץ קוֹרְדִים · תַּחַת הַנַּעֲצוּץ יַעֲלֶה בְרוֹשׁ וְתַחַת הַסִּרְפַּד יַעֲלֶה הֲדַס׃ מַקְשִׁיב דְּבַר שֶׁקֶר כְּתַב שִׂטְנָה וְעָצַב · נִתְעַטֵּף בְּבִגְדֵי שְׂרָד כְּיַעַד

en.text: Our God and the God of our fathers. When a certain man rose against us, fear and trembling took hold upon us; when he was associated with a king fond of adulation, we had well nigh succumbed. They determined to sell us, who were without any stay, like a heap of sand to fill up a moat; they said, “Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation, that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” Then our eyes were raised towards heaven, and we called upon thee to accurse such enemies, to cut off their name, and blot out their memory, and to extirpate them, to let my adversaries suffer for their malice, and let them be caught in the wiles which they deceitfully devised, saying, “The Lord shall not see it, neither shall the God of Jacob regard it.” But we reply, Though he afflict the scattered, and grieve them, yet he is not willing to consume them. For their former secret sins the Lord chastised them, making the king take off his signet, to terrify them, though it was only in appearance. For he performed his kind promise to exalt them in the eyes of the nations, and did not cast them away or abhor them to destroy them utterly in the land of their enemies. A hint of these events was given to the numerous and dispersed people in Deuteronomy, the word Hester there referring to Esther, and in the word Morderor in Exodus alluding to Mordecai; again the sudden end of Haman is indicated in Joshua, and his death on the gallows is hinted at in Genesis. Instead of the thorn (Haman) came up the fir-tree (Mordecai), and instead of the brier (Vashti) came up the myrtle tree (Esther).
